Part 1: Before Monday's meeting (30 Oct to 2 Nov)

Chapter 2 of 28

Presentation guide: the slides for Monday's call

When and how long: Friday evening, 20 minutes. Practise sharing on Teams once.

Your 6 slides

The deck you share on Teams if Prof. Zheng wants it. Open the PDF.

Meeting: Monday 2 November 2026, 17:00 to 17:30 Japan time = 13:30 to 14:00 India time, Microsoft Teams. The link is in Prof. Zheng's email of 30 Oct ("Online meeting (Mr. Sudhanshu Pandit)"). Prof. Zheng wrote that he wants "to discuss your research plan and the application process". Prof. Dohi and Prof. Okamura are in copy.

Files in this folder:

  • Sudhanshu_Pandit_Hiroshima_Zheng_meeting.pdf: present this one.
  • Sudhanshu_Pandit_Hiroshima_Zheng_meeting.pptx: the editable deck.
  • FULL_SCRIPT.md: what to say, from hello to goodbye.
  • MOCK_INTERVIEW.md: give this to a friend for a practice run.

Every number on the slides matches the proposal you sent him (01_Your_Documents/Research_Proposal_Hiroshima_Sudhanshu_Pandit.pdf).

1. Slides or no slides?

This is a 30-minute chat, not a talk. He did not ask for slides. So:

  • Let him lead. He will probably start with "Please tell me about your research" or go straight to the application.
  • Offer once: "I prepared six short slides on my plan, about five minutes. Would it help if I share my screen? Or I can just talk you through it."
  • If he says no, talk through it without slides. The Cue lines in FULL_SCRIPT.md are your talking points.
  • Keep the slides to 5 minutes, so there is time for his questions and the application.

2. How to share on Teams (practise once before Monday)

  1. Before the call, open the PDF in Preview. Close other apps. Turn on Do Not Disturb.
  2. Join at 13:25 IST. Camera on. Greet him first, without sharing.
  3. If he wants the slides: in Teams click Share (the arrow-in-a-box icon at the top), then choose the Preview window (not your whole screen). In Preview press Cmd + Shift + F for full screen. Use the arrow keys.
  4. Keep the script and your notes on your phone or on paper, never in the shared window.
  5. After slide 6, stop sharing so he sees your face.
  6. If sharing fails: "Sorry, let me just tell you," and use the Cue lines. He already has the PDF.

If you have never used Teams on this Mac: install the Teams app today, or test the link in Chrome, and check the camera and mic in Teams settings.

3. The six slides in one line each

# Slide What it is for
1 Title The question in one sentence: runs that share one rules file, do they fail together?
2 About me Degree, Layerpath, BrandMemory, Yuki 2.0, full time from April
3 Background Eckhardt and Lee; his own N-version paper; the two 2026 studies (429 vs about 115; 0.43 and 0.27); why a shared rules file matters
4 Two research questions RQ1 shared failures (beta-binomial ρ); RQ2 one rule, beyond the tests
5 Design Real PRs, 5 rules x 2 tasks, 10 runs per setting, 820 runs, 420 to 590 USD, 10,000+ inputs, the vote formula
6 Plan and why this lab Courses first, pilot, main runs, model, paper; his lab's probabilistic evaluation

The full words are in FULL_SCRIPT.md.

4. The 20 questions most likely after the slides

Short answers are in 03_Research_Plan_Defense/05_question_bank_with_model_answers.md (Q1 to Q15 and the follow-ups). The ones to practise out loud:

  1. Can you explain your research in a few sentences? (Q1)
  2. Why reliability? Why research, and why now? (Q2)
  3. Have you read our N-version paper? How is your work different? (Q3: only the abstract; ask him for a copy)
  4. Why can't you assume the runs fail independently? (Q4: p² + Var θ)
  5. How would voting work with code patches? (Q5: 3θ² minus 2θ³)
  6. Why a beta-binomial model, and how will you fit it? (Q6)
  7. How will you find failures that the tests miss? (Q7)
  8. What do you know about probability, statistics and NHPP models? (Q8: BCS301; honest)
  9. Is this realistic in two years, in time and money? (Q9)
  10. What are your programming skills? (Q10)
  11. Do you speak Japanese? (Q11: beginner, below N5)
  12. How will you pay for your studies? (Q12: self-funded)
  13. Why Hiroshima, and why this lab? (Q13)
  14. You would start in April. What about your job? (Q14)
  15. Are you applying anywhere else? (Q15: yes, NAIST for October 2027; be honest)
  16. Why 10 runs per setting? (follow-ups)
  17. What if every run passes every input? (follow-ups)
  18. Why not conversation history reuse, like in our paper? (follow-ups)
  19. How do you know removing the rule changed what the agent did? (follow-ups)
  20. Can you set the temperature in Claude Code or Codex? (follow-ups)

5. The application part of the call

He also wants to discuss the application. Have these open:

  • 05_Application/01_application_process_and_dates.md: dates, UCARO, documents, fees.
  • 05_Application/02_documents_checklist.md: who gives what.
  • The Consent Form: 05_Application/forms/5_Consent_Form_Sudhanshu_Pandit.docx.
  • The research plan form: 05_Application/forms/1_Research_Plan_Sudhanshu_Pandit.pdf.

Ask him about the Consent Form, whether he will review the research plan form, and anything to read before April (see 02_Meeting_Strategy/02_questions_to_ask_him.md).

6. Rehearsal plan

  • Today or Saturday: read FULL_SCRIPT.md out loud twice with the slides open (20 minutes). Practise sharing the Preview window on Teams once.
  • Sunday: the mock interview with a friend (MOCK_INTERVIEW.md, 30 minutes). Then Q1 to Q9 out loud until they feel easy.
  • Monday morning: the script once more, the call checklist in 02_Meeting_Strategy/03_day_of_checklist.md, and join at 13:25 IST.
